digest.top_line: ASTRO-ASCO-SSO PMRT guideline: PMRT strongly recommended for pN1, any pT4, ypN1 and cT4/cN2-3 after NST; conditional for pT3N0; moderate hypofractionation preferred.
digest.tldr: Breast carried the day: one joint guideline sets PMRT indications by pathologic and post-NST stage; another says RT should not be withheld in BRCA1/2, ATM or moderate-penetrance carriers, but intact-breast RT is contraindicated in germline TP53. HyTEC models put VS SRS 3-5y TCP at 91.2% at 12 Gy and adrenal SBRT 1-yr LC >95% at BED10 116.4 Gy.

sites.intro: Two joint ASTRO/ASCO/SSO guidelines: PMRT indications after upfront mastectomy or NST, and RT decisions in germline carriers.

studies.name: ASCO-ASTRO-SSO Hereditary Breast Cancer Guideline
studies.tldr: Joint consensus guideline: RT should not be withheld in BRCA1/2, ATM or other moderate-penetrance carriers; intact-breast RT is contraindicated in germline TP53 carriers.
details: 🔍 Joint ASCO/ASTRO/SSO guideline built on a systematic review plus a formal consensus process
🔍 58 articles informed the local therapy recs; 28 of them addressed RT in germline carriers
🔍 6 RCTs informed the systemic therapy recs

details.text: 📊 Radiation and local therapy recommendations by genotype

rows: BRCA status should not preclude BCT
RT not withheld for mutation status, after BCT or when PMRT is considered
Offer RT when clinically indicated; discuss data with ATM carriers considering BCT
Intact-breast RT contraindicated; mastectomy recommended; PMRT only with significant LRR risk
Offer CRRM; lowers CBC risk, survival benefit unproven
CRRM decision not driven mainly by mutation status
No routine platinum added to anthracycline + taxane
Olaparib or talazoparib as alternative to chemo, lines 1-3
No robust data supporting PARP inhibitors
Insufficient data to recommend a PARP inhibitor

details: 🔗 No evidence of a significant increase in toxicity or CBC from RT in BRCA1/2 or moderate-penetrance carriers
⚠️ ATM signal: one reviewed study reported higher CBC with RT in carriers of rare predicted-deleterious ATM variants; not consistent across studies
⚠️ ATM variant pathogenicity is unsettled; most ATM variants are missense, which confounds RT-risk studies
⚠️ CHEK2 1100delC is the only moderate-penetrance gene with CBC data: ~3-fold risk, 10% to 12% absolute at 10 years
🔍 Round 1 agreement ranged 72% to 98% (mean 90%); 1 of 17 recs missed the 75% threshold, passed at 90% on revote

verdict.rationale: Consensus guideline; most local therapy recs rest on formal consensus over low-to-intermediate observational evidence, so it allocates recommendations rather than reporting an outcome.
verdict.audience: Breast cancer with germline BRCA1/2, PALB2, CHEK2, ATM or TP53 mutation

studies.significance: The ATM recommendation carries only low evidence: RT should be offered when indicated because toxicity data are limited and inconsistent, and the one CBC signal involved rare predicted-deleterious variants of uncertain pathogenicity. TP53 is the only genotype where the guideline moves the RT decision, toward mastectomy with PMRT reserved for significant LRR risk.
studies.monday_clinic: In a Li-Fraumeni (germline TP53) pt with newly diagnosed breast cancer, this supports mastectomy over breast conservation with PMRT only for significant LRR risk; it does not support withholding RT from BRCA1/2, PALB2, CHEK2 or ATM carriers.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Joint ASCO/ASTRO/SSO guideline built on a systematic review and a **formal consensus process**. **58 articles** informed the local therapy questions (28 on RT) and **6 RCTs** informed the systemic questions. Two rounds of panel voting, with 47 to 49 respondents per recommendation.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Women with hereditary breast cancer, early or advanced, carrying germline **BRCA1/2, PALB2, CHEK2 or ATM** mutations, with separate guidance for **TP53**. Management is meant to be largely the same for men.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: **RT should not be withheld** because of mutation status after BCT or when PMRT is considered (Rec 6.1, strong). ATM carriers should be offered RT when clinically indicated (Rec 6.2, low evidence). Germline TP53: **intact-breast RT contraindicated**, PMRT only with significant LRR risk (Rec 6.3).

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Round 1 agreement ranged **72% to 98%** (mean 90%). Only the moderate-penetrance CRRM recommendation missed the 75% threshold; it was revised and passed at 90% (n=50) on the second round.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: The systemic recommendations rest on named RCTs: TNT for platinum over docetaxel, and OlympiAD and EMBRACA for olaparib and talazoparib. BROCADE-3 was presented too late to be incorporated: veliparib added to carboplatin-paclitaxel improved mPFS 14.5 v 12.6 mo (HR 0.71), with no significant OS difference.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents breast cancer pts with germline BRCA1/2 or moderate-penetrance (PALB2, CHEK2, ATM) mutations, plus germline TP53 for the RT contraindication. Does not represent tumor-only (somatic) BRCA mutations or other high-penetrance syndromes such as PTEN, STK11 and CDH1.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: In TNT, only 11 carriers had ER-positive disease, so the platinum preference extrapolates poorly to ER+ carriers. CBC risk data outside BRCA1/2 exist only for CHEK2 1100delC. Risk may be variant-specific (CHEK2 I157T vs 1100delC, ATM c.7271T>G), which the recommendations cannot resolve.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The RT recommendations are permissive by design: they remove genotype as a reason to avoid RT except for TP53, because evidence of harm is absent rather than disproven. For ATM, how carefully the data are discussed with the pt matters as much as the recommendation itself.

studies.interpretation:
For a radiation oncologist, the practical weight of this guideline sits in three recommendations: 6.1, 6.2 and 6.3. Their evidence bases differ more than their wording suggests. Rec 6.1 is graded strong on intermediate evidence: no significant increase in toxicity or contralateral cancer from RT among BRCA1/2 or moderate-penetrance carriers. This is a statement about the absence of a detected harm across a largely observational literature, and the panel turned it into a permissive default. That is the right direction, because withholding indicated RT has a known cost in local control, while the feared cost in carriers has not materialized in the data reviewed.

The ATM recommendation is where confidence should be lowest. Biallelic ATM loss (ataxia telangiectasia) confers clear radiosensitivity, and that biology drives the clinical worry about heterozygotes. The guideline is candid that the human data are thin. There are case reports of toxicity in heterozygous carriers, one reviewed study found more contralateral cancers after RT in carriers of rare predicted-deleterious variants, and that finding has not replicated. The confounder is classification: most ATM variants are missense, and pathogenicity calls differ, so studies may be pooling true loss-of-function alleles with benign variation. The low evidence grade is honest. A reader who sees a specific truncating or known high-risk ATM variant has a reasonable basis to have a fuller conversation, and the guideline encourages exactly that discussion with BCT candidates.

TP53 is the one genotype where the guideline changes the RT plan, and the logic is risk of induced malignancy rather than acute toxicity. Mastectomy becomes the recommended operation so the intact breast is never irradiated, and PMRT is reserved for significant LRR risk. That is a judgment call the guideline leaves to the treating team, without a threshold.

On the surgical interface, the guideline separates control of the index cancer from contralateral risk. BCT gives BRCA1/2 carriers local control of the index cancer similar to noncarriers, so the mastectomy discussion is driven by contralateral and new ipsilateral primary risk, with age at diagnosis as the strongest predictor. For moderate-penetrance carriers the guideline warns against extrapolating BRCA-level risks. Outside CHEK2 1100delC, there are essentially no contralateral risk data.

What this does not settle: whether ATM risk is variant-specific, the true contralateral cancer risk for PALB2 and ATM carriers, and whether any systemic advantage seen in BRCA-related disease extends to moderate-penetrance genes. Most of the local therapy recommendations are formal consensus over modest evidence, so they are best read as a reasoned default, not a measured effect.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Genotype changes the RT decision only for TP53: intact-breast RT is contraindicated, and PMRT is reserved for significant LRR risk. For BRCA1/2 and moderate-penetrance carriers, Rec 6.1 (strong) says RT is not withheld. ATM carriers get RT when indicated, on low-quality evidence.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: In platinum-naive metastatic gBRCA disease, platinum is preferred over taxane. Olaparib or talazoparib is an alternative to chemo in lines 1-3 for HER2-negative disease (high evidence, strong). No data support adding platinum in the (neo)adjuvant setting, PARP inhibitors in nonmetastatic disease, or PARP inhibitors in moderate-penetrance carriers.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: BCT stays on the table for BRCA1/2 carriers and should be offered to moderate-penetrance carriers. Nipple-sparing mastectomy is a reasonable option in both groups. CRRM is offered to BRCA1/2 carriers with age at diagnosis as the strongest CBC predictor, but is not driven mainly by genotype in moderate-penetrance genes.

open_questions: Is RT toxicity or CBC risk variant-specific in ATM carriers?
CBC risk for PALB2, ATM and non-1100delC CHEK2 carriers
PARP inhibitor efficacy in moderate-penetrance gene carriers

studies.name: ASTRO-ASCO-SSO PMRT Guideline
studies.tldr: PMRT is recommended for pN1, any pT4, ypN1 and cT4/cN2-3 after NST, and conditional for pT3N0 and cT1-3N1/cT3N0 ypN0. Moderate hypofractionation is preferred.
details: 🔍 Joint ASTRO-ASCO-SSO task force, 4 key questions: upfront mastectomy, post-NST, volumes/fractionation, technique
🔍 Systematic review Jan 2005 to Oct 15, 2024; 110 studies included (104 initial + 6 updated)
🔍 Retrospective studies excluded for KQ1; inclusion required ≥50 pts for RCTs and ≥100 pts for nonrandomized studies

details.text: 📊 KQ1: PMRT after mastectomy as initial treatment

rows: PMRT recommended, even without other risk factors

details.text: 📊 KQ2: PMRT after neoadjuvant systemic therapy

rows: Chest wall/reconstructed breast + RNI (axilla, SCV/ICV, IMN)

details: 📊 Technique: CT-based 3D-CRT; IMRT only when 3D-CRT can't meet goals; DIBH for normal tissue sparing
📊 Bolus for skin involvement, positive superficial margins and/or LVI; routine tissue-equivalent bolus not recommended

subdetails: pN1mic or low-burden pN1a after ALND with favorable features: omission may be appropriate
Favorable = pT1-2, low-intermediate grade, HR+/HER2-, postmenopausal, no LVI, low 21-gene RS
pT3N0 favorable: omit or chest wall alone
ypT0N0 after cT1-3N1/cT3N0: PMRT may be omitted
IMN coverage individualized by tumor location, size, nodal extent

details: ⚠️ Dose/fraction schedules not specified in source excerpt; 'moderate hypofractionation' left undefined here
⚠️ pN1 benefit rests on EBCTCG trials initiated by 1995, before modern HER2-directed therapy and IO
⚠️ Positive-margin recommendations rest on expert opinion only

verdict.rationale: Clinical practice guideline built on systematic review and graded consensus; no new efficacy endpoint. Codifies post-NST ypN status as the PMRT gate and hypofractionation as preferred.
verdict.audience: Adults with breast cancer undergoing mastectomy, upfront or post-NST

studies.significance: The ypN0 split is the new operating rule: cT1-3N1 or cT3N0 converting to ypN0 is conditional (omission reasonable at ypT0N0), while cT1-2N0 ypN0 is a strong no. Moderate hypofractionation is now strongly recommended even with reconstruction, and routine bolus is out, restricting it to skin involvement, superficial margins or LVI.
studies.monday_clinic: In cT1-3N1 or cT3N0 disease converting to ypN0 after neoadjuvant therapy, this supports a shared decision on PMRT, with omission reasonable at ypT0N0; it does not extend to cT4 or cN2-3 presentations, where PMRT stays indicated regardless of response.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Joint **ASTRO-ASCO-SSO** guideline from a systematic review of MEDLINE/Embase, Jan 2005 through Oct 15, 2024; **110 studies** included. Recommendations graded by strength (strong/conditional) and quality of evidence (high/moderate/low/expert opinion).

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Adults (age ≥18) with breast cancer undergoing mastectomy. Excludes inflammatory disease, DCIS, recurrent disease, reirradiation, oligometastatic/palliative settings, phyllodes and sarcoma.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: PMRT volume = **chest wall/reconstructed breast + regional nodes** including IMN, with chest wall alone allowed in select pT3N0. **Moderate hypofractionation preferred**; conventional fractionation acceptable with reconstruction or in rare cases. Boost conditional for T4 or close/positive margins; nodal boost strong for unaddressed nodal disease.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Grids above. Strong-for: pN1, any pT4, cT4/cN2-3 post-NST, ypN1. **Strong-against:** pT1-2N0 and cT1-2N0 ypN0. Conditional: pT3N0 and cT1-3N1/cT3N0 ypN0.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: pN1 indication anchored to the EBCTCG meta-analysis, which the panel flags as predating modern systemic therapy. The post-NST ypN0 conditional rests on cited data including NSABP B-51/RTOG 1304, RAPCHEM and ACOSOG Z1071.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents adults undergoing mastectomy, upfront or after neoadjuvant systemic therapy. Does not represent inflammatory breast cancer, recurrent disease, reirradiation, or breast-conserving surgery.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Fractionation and technique recommendations do not specify dose schedules in the excerpt. Margin-driven and nodal-boost recommendations are expert opinion, and pT1-2N0 'not recommended' carries **Low** QoE despite a Strong grade.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The guideline moves the PMRT decision post-NST from clinical stage to **pathologic nodal response**, and endorses de-escalation for favorable low-burden pN1. It does not settle which ypN0 pts can safely skip RNI beyond ypT0N0, nor the role of genomic scores outside HR+/HER2-.

studies.interpretation:
The guideline makes the most consequential move in the neoadjuvant setting. For two decades the post-NST PMRT decision was anchored to clinical presentation, largely because the randomized PMRT literature was built in an upfront-surgery era. Here the panel shifts the gate to pathologic nodal response: ypN1 is a strong indication, cT1-2N0 converting to ypN0 is a strong recommendation against, and the large middle (cT1-3N1 or cT3N0 with ypN0) is conditional, with omission explicitly reasonable after ypT0N0. That structure is consistent with what NSABP B-51/RTOG 1304 was designed to test, and with the RAPCHEM registry and ACOSOG Z1071 analyses cited, but the panel grades the evidence for the conditional bucket as moderate rather than high, so the conditional label is honest rather than a hedge.

In the upfront setting the guideline keeps pN1 as a strong indication on high-quality evidence, yet it simultaneously acknowledges that the evidence base, the EBCTCG meta-analysis, comes from trials started by 1995 and before HER2-directed therapy and immunotherapy. The implementation remark allowing omission for pN1mic or low-burden pN1a after ALND with a favorable profile (pT1-2, low-intermediate grade, HR+/HER2-, postmenopausal, no LVI, low 21-gene score) is where the guideline quietly accommodates the de-escalation argument without changing the headline grade. A reader should notice that this remark is not graded, so it carries panel opinion rather than the high QoE of the recommendation above it.

The pT1-2N0 recommendation is an instructive mismatch: strong against PMRT, but on low-quality evidence. ASTRO methodology permits that when panel consensus is clear, and the carve-out for multiple unfavorable features (triple-negative, high grade, LVI, young age, central/medial tumors) leaves room for judgment. The same logic applies to positive margins, where both the upfront and post-NST recommendations rest on expert opinion.

For the RT reader, the technical recommendations are the more immediately actionable change. Moderate hypofractionation is strongly recommended without reconstruction (high QoE) and preferred with reconstruction (moderate QoE for hypofractionation), which removes reconstruction as a default reason to fractionate conventionally. Routine tissue-equivalent bolus is explicitly not recommended, limiting it to skin involvement, positive superficial margins or LVI, a departure from habit in many departments. IMRT is positioned as a fallback when 3D-CRT cannot meet goals, not a default, and DIBH is recommended.

What the document does not settle: the specific dose schedules behind 'moderate hypofractionation' are not in the excerpt, IMN coverage remains individualized rather than rule-based, and the guideline offers no biomarker framework for identifying which ypN0 pts can omit regional nodes beyond complete pathologic response. Those are the questions the next update will need prospective data to answer.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Hypofractionation is now strongly recommended even with reconstruction, routine bolus is out (reserved for skin involvement, superficial margins, LVI), and IMRT is a fallback to 3D-CRT. Post-NST, ypN status rather than clinical stage drives the RNI decision.
significance_by_specialty.medonc: Response to neoadjuvant systemic therapy directly changes the RT indication: ypT0N0 after cT1-3N1 or cT3N0 permits PMRT omission. A low 21-gene score counts as a favorable feature supporting omission in low-burden pN1 and pT3N0.
significance_by_specialty.surgonc: Post-NST nodal pathology now sets the PMRT call: ypN1 strong-for, cT1-2N0 ypN0 strong-against, cT1-3N1 ypN0 conditional. Positive mastectomy margins carry a PMRT recommendation on expert opinion, which feeds into reconstruction timing and margin planning.

open_questions: Which ypN0 pts beyond ypT0N0 can safely omit regional nodal RT?
Is PMRT omission safe in low-burden pN1 with modern systemic therapy?
Optimal hypofractionation schedule with implant reconstruction

sites.intro: HyTEC dose-response modeling for sporadic VS SRS, plus a LINAC replanning study where VMAT gains conformity at ~41% more MU.

studies.name: HyTEC Vestibular Schwannoma SRS TCP
studies.tldr: Pooled LQ model of 35 series (5162 pts) predicts 3-5y TCP 91.2% at 12 Gy and 93.5% at 13 Gy single-fraction SRS.
details: 🔍 HyTEC literature pooling: 35 publications, 5162 pts, sporadic VS only
🔍 TCP taken at 5y when reported, else 3y (21 articles 3y, 14 articles 5y)
📊 3-5y tumor control >90% to 95% in 89% of reviewed studies; 4 smaller studies at 80% to 90%
⚠️ No outcome data below the equivalent of 11 Gy x1; lower-dose predictions are extrapolation
⚠️ Only 46% of articles gave Kaplan-Meier estimates; the rest were crude control at median f/u
⚠️ Untreated TCP fixed at an assumed 30%; prescription dose treated as GTV minimum dose
🔍 NF2 excluded (TCP approximately 75% at 5y); pediatric and post-resection progression not modeled

verdict.rationale: Literature-level pooled model, not IPD: heterogeneous control definitions, crude incidence in most series, assumed untreated TCP, no dosimetric variables. Volume and NF2 not modeled.
verdict.audience: Sporadic vestibular schwannoma, adult, SRS or 3-5 fx fSRS

studies.significance: The usable read is the 1, 3 and 5 fx dose equivalence table: 95% TCP sits at 13.8-14.1 Gy x1, 18.8-19.2 Gy/3 and 21.5-23.0 Gy/5 across both models. Current 12-13 Gy, 18 Gy/3 and 25 Gy/5 prescriptions all land on the plateau. That supports picking fractionation on nerve and hearing goals rather than on tumor control.
studies.monday_clinic: For an adult with sporadic VS, these models put 12-13 Gy x1, 18 Gy/3 and 25 Gy/5 within a few points of each other on predicted 3-5y control; they do not extend to NF2-related tumors or to doses below the equivalent of 11 Gy x1.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: HyTEC pooled review of **35 publications, 5162 pts**, fit with a 3-parameter Poisson TCP model (α/β free) under both **LQ and LQ-L** dose conversion. 3-5y control pooled (3y in 21 articles, 5y in 14).

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Sporadic VS treated with SRS or fSRS. **NF2 excluded**; the authors also tried to exclude progression after prior resection, and pediatric pts were not analyzed.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Common prescriptions pooled: **12-13 Gy x1, 18-21 Gy/3, 25 Gy/5**. Prescription dose was assumed to be the GTV minimum dose; PTV margins and heterogeneity were not modeled.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: LQ fit: EQD2 50% 3.48 Gy, α/β 12.4 Gy. LQ-L fit: EQD2 50% 5.15 Gy, α/β 2.97 Gy, with a marginally better fit and tighter CIs. Both fits P < .0001.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: The model places contemporary low-dose single-fraction practice at the 12-13 Gy marginal dose and the common 3 and 5 fx schedules at **similar 3-5y TCP**, consistent with the cited literature that found SRS and fractionated SRT about equally effective.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents adult sporadic VS treated with 1-5 fx SRS at ≥11 Gy single-fraction equivalent. Does not represent NF2-related tumors, pediatric pts, repeat SRS, or doses below the equivalent of 11 Gy x1.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: Only **26%** of reports gave conformity indices, so volume could not partition TCP. Most series run 3-5y and few pass 10y, which leaves late regrowth uncharacterized.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The α/β is model-dependent (12.4 vs 2.97 Gy), so any conversion between fractionations carries that uncertainty. Table 2's reporting standards (KM with full curves, GTV/PTV definitions, Dxx/Vxx, 6-category volumetric outcome) are the authors' fix for the data gap.

studies.interpretation:
The value here is less a new answer than a calibration of an old one. Single-fraction VS radiosurgery has drifted down to a 12-13 Gy marginal dose to protect hearing and the facial and trigeminal nerves, and the open worry has been whether that de-escalation gave up tumor control. Pooled across 5162 pts, the LQ model puts 12 Gy at 91.2% and 13 Gy at 93.5% 3-5y TCP, and the LQ-L model puts them higher still, at 95.6% and 97.33%. Both readings say the modern single-fraction dose sits on the shoulder of the curve rather than its steep part, so a further step down would cost control faster than the step from 13 to 12 Gy did.

The fractionation comparison is the more practical result. 18 Gy/3 and 25 Gy/5 predict 93.6% and 97.2% (LQ) or 94.0% and 96.9% (LQ-L), which is within a few points of the single-fraction regimens under either model. That matters because the choice between SRS and fSRS for a larger tumor, or one abutting the brainstem or cochlea, is usually made on toxicity grounds. The model offers no tumor-control reason to avoid the fractionated schedules in common use. The 95% TCP physical-dose table gives a planning reference that holds up under both models better than any single α/β does.

Confidence should be tempered by how the inputs were built. This is a fit to published summary points, not to patient-level data. Fewer than half the series reported Kaplan-Meier estimates, so many points are crude control at median follow-up, which inflates control when follow-up is short. Definitions of failure differed (radiologic growth, symptoms, need for salvage), and post-SRS pseudoprogression makes radiologic failure especially soft in VS. The untreated control rate was fixed at 30% by assumption, and the curve below the equivalent of 11 Gy x1 is pure extrapolation, which is the dose range where the de-escalation question would actually be decided.

The α/β disagreement is the clearest warning. LQ returns 12.4 Gy and LQ-L 2.97 Gy for the same tumor, and the authors favor LQ-L as closer to radiobiological intuition for a slow-growing benign lesion. A reader converting an unusual fractionation should treat the LQ estimate as the optimistic bound for fSRS equivalence. Because target volume could not be modeled, the curve also says nothing about whether a 3 cm tumor needs more dose than an intracanalicular one, which is the question most clinicians face when choosing between 1 and 5 fractions.

What would overturn the read is long-term data. Most series stop at 5y, while untreated VS keeps growing for a decade, so late failures after low-dose SRS could pull the plateau down. The reporting template in Table 2 (volumetric trajectories, Dxx/Vxx for failures versus controls, KM with numbers at risk) is the route to a volume-stratified, dosimetry-aware model, and it is arguably the paper's most lasting contribution.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The 95% TCP dose equivalents (13.8-14.1 Gy x1, 18.8-19.2 Gy/3, 21.5-23.0 Gy/5) put current 1, 3 and 5 fx prescriptions on the same plateau. That lets fractionation follow hearing and cranial nerve goals. Do not lean on predictions below 11 Gy x1, which are extrapolation.

open_questions: Does TCP depend on tumor volume at fixed dose?
Durability of control beyond 10 years after low-dose SRS

studies.name: LINAC SRS: DCA vs VMAT Dosimetric Study
studies.tldr: Paddick CI 0.78 VMAT vs 0.75 DCA+SSO+VDR (p=0.03); GI and V12Gy not different between the two; VMAT ~41 ± 17% more MU.
details: 🔍 Retrospective replanning study, 11 brain cases, 4 plans each on Monaco TPS (v.5.11.03)

subdetails: 7 solitary mets, 2 meningioma, 1 acoustic schwannoma, 1 pituitary adenoma
PTV volume 0.93 to 22.5 cc (median 4.99cc); PTV = GTV + 2 mm
6 FFF, Agility MLC with 5 mm leaves, Monte Carlo, 0.3 cm grid

details: ⚠️ Geometry confounded: all DCA plans noncoplanar, VMAT single-arc coplanar only

details.text: 📊 Mean plan metrics by technique (paired t-test, sequential comparisons)

columns: p (DCA vs SSO, SSO vs VDR, VDR vs VMAT)

details: 📊 VMAT V12Gy lower than every DCA variant in 9 of 11 pts
⚠️ No delivery time measured; authors' claim of shorter VMAT treatment time is unquantified
⚠️ Multiple paired t-tests, no correction; only adjacent techniques compared, never DCA vs VMAT directly
⚠️ V12Gy reported across SRS and SRT cases alike, though it is a single-fraction metric
🔗 Authors cite Chang et al: VMAT needed higher MU than DCA by a factor of 2.37

verdict.rationale: Dosimetric replanning only, N=11 mixed histologies; technique confounded with coplanar vs noncoplanar geometry; uncorrected multiple paired t-tests; no delivery-time or clinical endpoints.
verdict.audience: Single intracranial SRS/SRT target, 0.93 to 22.5 cc, LINAC-based

studies.significance: Against fully optimized DCA (SSO + VDR), coplanar VMAT bought only a CI gain of 0.75 to 0.78, with GI (p=0.29) and brain V12Gy (p=0.38) not different, at 41 ± 17% more MU. Because DCA was noncoplanar and VMAT coplanar, this compares beam geometry as much as optimization, which limits any class-solution claim.
studies.monday_clinic: For a single intracranial target planned on an Elekta Agility LINAC, this supports DCA+SSO+VDR as a dosimetric near-equivalent to coplanar VMAT on gradient and V12Gy; it does not address multi-lesion SRS, noncoplanar VMAT, or clinical radionecrosis outcomes.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: Retrospective dosimetric replanning of **11 brain cases**, each planned with DCA, DCA+SSO, DCA+SSO+VDR and VMAT. Paired t-tests between adjacent techniques, p<0.05 significant.

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: 7 solitary metastases, 2 meningiomas, 1 acoustic schwannoma, 1 pituitary adenoma. **9 SRS and 2 SRT**, PTV 0.93 to 22.5 cc (median 4.99cc).

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Prescription **18 to 30Gy**; PTV = GTV + 2 mm; objective 95% of PTV covered by 95% of prescription. 6 FFF on Agility MLC (5 mm leaves); **DCA noncoplanar** with couch angles spaced at least 30 degrees, **VMAT single coplanar arc**, max 180 control points.

analysis_sections.label: Endpoints
analysis_sections.body: Paddick CI, Paddick GI, RTOG HI, MU as a treatment-time proxy, and normal brain V12Gy. No delivery time, QA pass rate or clinical endpoint.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: Stepwise gains from DCA through SSO and VDR; VMAT edged DCA+SSO+VDR on CI only (**p=0.03**), with **no difference in GI or V12Gy** and **41 ± 17% more MU**.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: Direction matches the cited Lagerwaard et al (vestibular schwannoma) and Chang et al series favoring VMAT on CI and GI. Consistent with Rudd et al that DCA yields better HI in smaller tumors.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents single-target LINAC SRS/SRT with 5 mm-leaf MLC and Monaco Monte Carlo planning. Does not represent multi-metastasis single-isocenter SRS, noncoplanar VMAT, or Gamma Knife and CyberKnife planning.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: 5 mm leaves are coarse for sub-cc targets, which likely penalizes DCA conformity in the smallest PTVs. V12Gy was pooled across 2 SRT cases where it is not the relevant metric, and DCA was never tested directly against VMAT.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The defensible read is that a fully optimized DCA (SSO + VDR) closes most of the gap to VMAT, and the remaining CI difference is small. Whether that gap matters clinically, or survives noncoplanar VMAT, is untested here.

studies.interpretation:
The headline that VMAT is the preferred SRS technique is narrower than it sounds. The comparison that matters to a planner is not plain DCA against VMAT, which is a straw man in modern practice, but fully optimized DCA (segment shape optimization plus variable dose rate) against VMAT. On that comparison the paper shows a conformity index of 0.75 versus 0.78, gradient index 1.20 versus 1.17 with p=0.29, and brain V12Gy 11.75 versus 11.14cc with p=0.38. In other words, VMAT's only statistically separable advantage over optimized DCA is a modest conformity gain, while it costs 41 ± 17% more MU. Gradient index and V12Gy, the two metrics most tied to radionecrosis risk in single-fraction SRS, did not distinguish the techniques.

The design confounds two variables. Every DCA plan used noncoplanar beams and every VMAT plan used a single coplanar arc. Noncoplanar geometry is usually expected to improve dose falloff, so the fact that coplanar VMAT still matched optimized DCA on gradient is mildly interesting, but it also means the study cannot attribute any difference to inverse optimization versus beam arrangement. A noncoplanar VMAT arm, which many centers now use for single targets, is absent, and that is the comparison a reader choosing a class solution actually needs.

Several methodological choices should lower confidence further. Eleven cases spanning metastases and three benign histologies, two of them fractionated, is a small and heterogeneous set; pooling V12Gy across SRS and SRT cases mixes a single-fraction constraint with plans where it does not apply. The statistics compare only adjacent techniques in a chain, so DCA versus VMAT is never formally tested, and five or more uncorrected paired t-tests per metric make borderline p-values such as 0.03 fragile. The Agility MLC's 5 mm leaves are coarse for targets under 1 cc, which plausibly penalizes the forward-planned DCA variants most in the smallest lesions. Finally, the conclusion that VMAT shortens overall treatment time is asserted from FFF dose rate rather than measured, and the paper also notes that noncoplanar DCA requires room entry for couch rotations, so true delivery time is the open variable.

Against the cited literature, including Chang et al and Lagerwaard et al, the direction is consistent: VMAT improves conformity and gradient over simple DCA. What this study adds is that the incremental vendor options on an Elekta Versa HD recover most of that advantage. The practical reading is permissive rather than prescriptive: a center without VMAT, or one preferring DCA for its lower modulation and smaller sensitivity to setup error, has dosimetric support here. What would make the paper's own conclusion wrong is a noncoplanar VMAT comparison, a larger single-histology cohort, or clinical radionecrosis data showing the conformity difference carries no outcome weight.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: Against fully optimized DCA (SSO + VDR), coplanar VMAT gained only a CI of 0.75 to 0.78, with GI (p=0.29) and brain V12Gy (p=0.38) not different, at 41 ± 17% more MU. DCA was noncoplanar and VMAT coplanar, so the result compares beam geometry as much as optimization.

open_questions: Does noncoplanar VMAT outperform optimized noncoplanar DCA?
Do CI differences of this size change radionecrosis risk?
Does the ranking hold for multi-lesion single-isocenter SRS?

sites.intro: HyTEC adrenal SBRT fit built on small retrospective series; the 1-yr LC endpoint may understate underdosing.

studies.name: HyTEC Adrenal SBRT TCP
studies.tldr: 1-yr LC >95% predicted at BED10 116.4 Gy (EQD2 ~97 Gy) in a Poisson TCP fit to published adrenal metastasis SBRT series.
details: 📊 Model: 1-yr LC >95% at BED10 116.4 Gy (EQD2 ~97 Gy)
🔍 Literature review 2007-2017: 250 hits, small retrospective series of 6-49 lesions each
🔍 Dose per study = median Rx adjusted for IDL when known; no DVH data
💊 Across series: median 40 Gy (mean 37.2 Gy), median 5 fx (range 1-27)

details.text: 📊 Fractionations the authors give as examples near the target
subdetails: Casamassima: 36 Gy / 3 fx to 70% IDL, BED10 just over 139 Gy at isocenter, LC 90% at 1 and 2 yr

details.text: 🔗 Predicted 1-yr LC by BED10, in-press meta-analysis (22 studies), within this model's CI

details: 🔗 Later series at BED10 112.5 Gy: 96.5% 1-yr LC (31 pts, 33 lesions), on the curve
⚠️ Series at BED10 85.5 and 72 Gy lost LC at 2-3 yr; a 1-yr endpoint understates underdosing
⚠️ Crude 1-yr LC ranged 44% to 100% across series; competing death from other mets lowers its reliability
⚠️ OS fit (χ2 44.7, P<.001) has wide CIs; dose likely tracks selection, not causation
🔍 No PTV margin or IDL (70-100%) correlation with LC; margins ranged 0 to 10 mm

verdict.rationale: Ecological fit: one study-level median dose vs crude 1-yr LC per series, no DVH data, small retrospective single-institution cohorts with mixed histology and competing mortality.
verdict.audience: Adrenal metastases treated with SBRT, no prior adrenal RT

studies.significance: The 116.4 Gy figure is a GTV-coverage estimate: study medians were adjusted for the prescription IDL, so it describes how well the plan covers gross disease, not the nominal Rx line. The series at BED10 85.5 and 72 Gy held 1-yr LC but lost it at 2-3 yr, so the argument for escalating rests on durability.
studies.monday_clinic: For an adrenal metastasis being planned for SBRT with motion management, this supports a GTV-coverage BED10 near 116.4 Gy where OAR tolerances allow. It does not extend to adrenal reirradiation, which is represented by only 2 pts.

analysis_sections.label: Design
analysis_sections.body: HyTEC literature review and **Poisson TCP model**. PubMed search covered 2007 to 2017. 1-yr LC was fit by maximum likelihood, with CIs from profile likelihood. Each study contributed its **median prescription dose**, IDL-adjusted when known, converted to EQD2 (α/β 10).

analysis_sections.label: Population & inclusion
analysis_sections.body: Small single-institution, mostly retrospective series of **6-49 lesions** each, with multiple primary histologies. All but 1 series excluded prior adrenal RT, and every series used respiratory motion management.

analysis_sections.label: Radiotherapy
analysis_sections.body: Across series: median **40 Gy in 5 fx** (range 1-27 fx), Rx to the 70-100% IDL. Most built a 4DCT ITV with a ~3-5 mm PTV margin. Median PTVs ranged 41 to 306.6 cm3.

analysis_sections.label: Results
analysis_sections.body: **1-yr LC >95% at BED10 116.4 Gy** (EQD2 ~97 Gy). LC fit χ2 57.5, P<.0001; D50 34.6 Gy EQD2, γ50 0.4996. The OS fit (χ2 44.7, P<.001; D50 44.7) had wide CIs. **No correlation** of PTV margin or IDL with LC.

analysis_sections.label: vs leading data
analysis_sections.body: This matches the **BED10 ≥100 Gy** LC association the authors cite from early-stage NSCLC SBRT. Three later series fell within the model's 95% CI, and an in-press 22-study meta-analysis predicts 92.9% 1-yr LC at BED10 100 Gy. NRG-BR001 (phase 1) prescribes 45 Gy/3 fx.

analysis_sections.label: Applies to
analysis_sections.body: Represents adrenal metastases receiving SBRT with motion management and image guidance. Does not represent adrenal reirradiation or a direct comparison with adrenalectomy.

analysis_sections.label: Limitations
analysis_sections.body: RECIST may misread SBRT response, and three series used PET/CT progression instead. Fitting 1-yr LC hides later failures: the series at **BED10 85.5 and 72 Gy** lost control at 2-3 yr.

analysis_sections.label: Discussion
analysis_sections.body: The model supports a **dose floor near BED10 116.4 Gy** to gross disease. It cannot say how to reach that dose next to bowel or stomach, and **no randomized data** compare SBRT with adrenalectomy.

studies.interpretation:
The value of this analysis is a dose target for a site where the evidence is a collection of small single-institution series whose prescriptions are hard to compare. Converting each series to an IDL-adjusted EQD2 and fitting 1-year local control produces a usable dose-response curve. Its headline threshold, BED10 116.4 Gy for more than 95% 1-year control, sits close to the BED10 ≥100 Gy convention the authors cite from early-stage NSCLC SBRT. That agreement is reassuring but partly circular: if the higher-dose adrenal series were already planned around lung-derived targets, a fit across them will tend to reproduce that target rather than test it independently.

The unit of analysis should lower a reader's confidence the most. Each study contributes one point: a median prescription dose set against a crude 1-year control rate, with no DVH data. That is an ecological fit. Within-study dose spread, lesion size, histology mix and the 70-100% IDL range all fold into scatter around a single point. The D50 of 34.6 Gy EQD2 has a 95% CI of 27.1 to 45.4, and the slope's interval is similarly broad. A >95% prediction sits on the shallow upper shoulder of the curve, where a small shift in the fitted parameters moves the dose needed a long way. Competing mortality also matters here. Many of these pts die of extra-adrenal disease before a local failure can be observed, which flatters crude 1-year control in poor-prognosis cohorts.

The external checks are the more persuasive part. Three series published during write-up fell within the model's confidence band, including one at BED10 112.5 Gy with 96.5% 1-year control. An in-press meta-analysis of 22 studies reaches predictions inside the same band. The two lower-dose series (BED10 85.5 and 72 Gy) are the most informative for practice: they held control at 1 year and lost it by 2 to 3 years. So the case for escalation is really about durability. A 1-year endpoint is the wrong ruler for a pt with oligometastatic disease and a long expected survival, and the true dose requirement for durable control may sit higher than this curve implies.

The OS fit should not be read as radiation driving survival. Dose in these series almost certainly tracks selection: smaller targets, fitter pts and fewer competing sites of disease all permit, and coincide with, higher prescriptions. The same selection problem makes the surgical comparison uninterpretable. The adrenalectomy review the authors discuss had a lower share of lung primaries and more isolated adrenal disease (75% vs 48%) than the SBRT cohorts.

What the paper settles is a reasonable planning goal for gross-disease coverage when OARs permit. It leaves open how to get there next to stomach, duodenum and kidney, whether margin or IDL choice matters (no correlation was detectable at this resolution), and what is safe for reirradiation. NRG-BR001, prescribing 45 Gy in 3 fx, is the nearest prospective data source for a dose in this range.

significance_by_specialty.radonc: The 116.4 Gy target is a GTV-coverage estimate built from IDL-adjusted study medians, so it applies to how a plan covers gross disease. The series at BED10 85.5 and 72 Gy lost LC at 2-3 yr, which makes durability, not the 1-yr number, the reason to push dose where OARs allow.

open_questions: SBRT vs adrenalectomy in comparable oligometastatic pts
Dose required for durable LC beyond 2 years

papers.title: Management of Hereditary Breast Cancer: American Society of Clinical Oncology, American Society for Radiation Oncology, and Society of Surgical Oncology Guideline
papers.abstract: PURPOSE To develop recommendations for management of patients with breast cancer (BC) with germline mutations in BC susceptibility genes. METHODS The American Society of Clinical Oncology, American Society for Radiation Oncology, and Society of Surgical Oncology convened an Expert Panel to develop recommendations based on a systematic review of the literature and a formal consensus process. RESULTS Fifty-eight articles met eligibility criteria and formed the evidentiary basis for the local therapy recommendations; six randomized controlled trials of systemic therapy met eligibility criteria. RECOMMENDATIONS Patients with newly diagnosed BC and BRCA1/ 2 mutations may be considered for breast-conserving therapy (BCT), with local control of the index cancer similar to that of noncarriers. The significant risk of a contralateral BC (CBC), especially in young women, and the higher risk of new cancers in the ipsilateral breast warrant discussion of bilateral mastectomy. Patients with mutations in moderate-risk genes should be offered BCT. For women with mutations in BRCA1/ 2 or moderate-penetrance genes who are eligible for mastectomy, nipple-sparing mastectomy is a reasonable approach. There is no evidence of increased toxicity or CBC events from radiation exposure in BRCA1/ 2 carriers. Radiation therapy should not be withheld in ATM carriers. For patients with germline TP53 mutations, mastectomy is advised; radiation therapy is contraindicated except in those with significant risk of locoregional recurrence. Platinum agents are recommended versus taxanes to treat advanced BC in BRCA carriers. In the adjuvant/neoadjuvant setting, data do not support the routine addition of platinum to anthracycline- and taxane-based chemotherapy. Poly (ADP-ribose) polymerase (PARP) inhibitors (olaparib and talazoparib) are preferable to nonplatinum single-agent chemotherapy for treatment of advanced BC in BRCA1/ 2 carriers. Data are insufficient to recommend PARP inhibitor use in the early setting or in moderate-penetrance carriers. Additional information available at www.asco.org/breast-cancer-guidelines .

papers.title: Postmastectomy Radiation Therapy: An ASTRO-ASCO-SSO Clinical Practice Guideline
papers.abstract: ASCO Guidelines provide recommendations with comprehensive review and analyses of the relevant literature for each recommendation, following the guideline development process as outlined in the ASCO Guidelines Methodology Manual . ASCO Guidelines follow the ASCO Conflict of Interest Policy for Clinical Practice Guidelines . Clinical Practice Guidelines and other guidance (“Guidance”) provided by ASCO is not a comprehensive or definitive guide to treatment options. It is intended for voluntary use by clinicians and should be used in conjunction with independent professional judgment. Guidance may not be applicable to all patients, interventions, diseases or stages of diseases. Guidance is based on review and analysis of relevant literature, and is not intended as a statement of the standard of care. ASCO does not endorse third-party drugs, devices, services, or therapies and assumes no responsibility for any harm arising from or related to the use of this information. See complete ASCO and ASTRO disclaimers in Appendix 1 (online only) for more. PURPOSE This guideline provides recommendations on use of postmastectomy radiation therapy (PMRT) in breast cancer treatment. Updated recommendations detail indications for PMRT in the upfront surgical setting and after neoadjuvant systemic therapy, and provide guidance on appropriate target volumes, dosing, and treatment techniques. METHODS A multidisciplinary American Society for Radiation Oncology–ASCO–Society of Surgical Oncology task force addressed four key radiation therapy (RT) questions in patients with breast cancer who undergo mastectomy: (1) indications for PMRT after upfront surgery, (2) indications for PMRT after neoadjuvant systemic therapy followed by surgery, (3) appropriate PMRT volumes and dose-fractionation regimens, and (4) treatment techniques. Recommendations were based on a systematic review and created using a predefined consensus-building methodology for quality of evidence grading and strength of recommendation. RECOMMENDATIONS After upfront mastectomy, PMRT is indicated for most patients with node-positive breast cancer and select patients with node-negative disease. PMRT is also recommended after neoadjuvant systemic therapy for patients presenting with locally advanced disease and for those with residual nodal disease at the time of surgery. PMRT is conditionally recommended for patients with cT1-3N1 or cT3N0 breast cancer with pathologically negative nodes after neoadjuvant systemic therapy (ypN0). When PMRT is delivered, treatment to the ipsilateral chest wall or reconstructed breast and regional lymphatics is recommended, with moderate hypofractionation preferred, but with conventional fractionation approaches acceptable in rare cases. Computed tomography–based volumetric treatment planning with 3-dimensional conformal RT is recommended, with intensity-modulated RT advised when three-dimensional conformal RT is unable to achieve treatment goals. Deep inspiration breath-hold techniques are also recommended for normal tissue sparing. For patients with skin involvement, positive superficial margins, and/or lymphovascular invasion, use of a bolus is recommended, but routine use of tissue-equivalent bolus is not recommended. Additional information is available at www.asco.org/breast-cancer-guidelines .

papers.title: Stereotactic Radiosurgery for Vestibular Schwannomas: Tumor Control Probability Analyses and Recommended Reporting Standards
Modeling of Tumor Control Probability in Stereotactic Body Radiation Therapy for Adrenal Tumors
The Optimal Choice of Technique for Stereotactic Radiosurgery—A LINAC-Based Dosimetric Study between DCA, DCA-SSO, DCA-SSO-VDR, and VMAT
papers.abstract: Abstract Introduction Advanced radiation therapy delivery techniques require greater understanding of various planning sequences and methods. The aim of this study is to determine a class solution that finds the best possible technique to deliver for stereotactic radiosurgery between dynamic conformal arc (DCA) techniques using various options such as DCA, DCA + SSO (segment shape optimization), and DCA + SSO + VDR (variable dose rate) using noncoplanar beam arrangement and volumetric modulated arc therapy (VMAT) using coplanar beams. Materials and Methods In this dosimetric study, 11 brain cases were retrospectively planned for various techniques and analyzed for the Paddick conformity index (CI), Radiation Therapy Oncology Group homogeneity index (HI), Paddick gradient index (GI), treatment time in terms of monitor units (MU) and normal brain dose (V12Gy). The paired t-test was performed to know the statistical significance between the techniques. Results In terms of CI, GI, and control of the normal brain dose, the VMAT plan was superior to other techniques. But, HI was found to be better with DCA. Above all, VMAT delivered higher MU than any other technique. The p-values between DCA + SSO and DCA, DCA + SSO + VDR and DCA + SSO, and VMAT and DCA + SSO + VDR are as follows: CI: 0.0004, 0.015, and 0.03; GI: 0.03, 0.33, and 0.29; HI: 0.008, 0.04, and 0.06; V12 Gy of normal brain: 0.1, 0.01, 0.38. VMAT requires approximately 41 ± 17% more MU than DCA + SSO + VDR. Conclusion VMAT using coplanar beams is preferable among all the techniques, considering the dosimetric parameters studied. If VMAT is not available in the facility, DCA + SSO + VDR technique using non coplanar beams can be used to deliver SRS treatment.
